english.title: Attempt to travel on railway without paying fare
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) attempted to travel on a railway, namely **(..SPECIFY NAME..), without having previously paid at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..) your fare of **(..SPECIFY AMOUNT..) and with intent to avoid payment thereof
english.legislation: Contrary to section 5(3)(a) of the Regulation of Railways Act 1889.

english.notes:
(i) If no intent to avoid the fare can be proved, consider subsection 5(1), fail to show ticket, pay fare, give name/address.
(ii) Payment of the fare means payment of the proper fare, so an offence can be committed by travelling first class on a standard class ticket. (Gillingham v Walker 1881 44 LT 715).
(iii) A demand for payment of the excess fare does not bar criminal proceedings. (Noble v Killick 1891 LJMC 61).
(iv) See also offence wording: H1584.

other.powersofarrest:
In England and Wales: Arrest without warrant.

In Scotland: Common Law powers of arrest apply.
other.penalty:
Three months imprisonment or a fine not exceeding level three on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
